deck_name: Visconti-Sforza Tarot — The Oldest Near-Complete Tarot (attr. Bonifacio Bembo, c. 1451)

major-00-il-matto.name: 0 — The Fool
major-00-il-matto.Scene: A ragged youth strides forward with a staff over his shoulder; feathers or leaves are tucked into his hair and he wears tattered clothing. His gaze is upward and his posture suggests purposeful wandering.

major-01-il-bagatto.name: 1 — The Magician
major-01-il-bagatto.Scene: A bearded man in a red and green pointed hat sits at a workbench or table covered with small objects; he appears to be demonstrating or manipulating the items laid before him.

major-02-la-papessa.name: 2 — The Popess
major-02-la-papessa.Scene: A crowned woman in papal robes is enthroned; she holds a closed book in one hand and a tall papal staff in the other. Her expression is composed and authoritative.

major-03-limperatrice.name: 3 — The Empress
major-03-limperatrice.Scene: A standing woman in gold brocade holds a heraldic shield bearing an eagle and wears blue angel wings; she faces forward with a commanding expression.

major-04-limperatore.name: 4 — The Emperor
major-04-limperatore.Scene: An elderly bearded man in blue robes is seated on a throne; he gestures with one hand and a small black eagle perches on his hat.

major-05-il-papa.name: 5 — The Pope
major-05-il-papa.Scene: A bearded pope in white and blue vestments is enthroned; he raises his right hand in a blessing gesture and holds a tall papal staff or triregnum.

major-06-lamore.name: 6 — The Lovers
major-06-lamore.Scene: A winged nude Cupid is suspended in midair above; below, a young man in courtly dress stands between two women, one of whom reaches toward him or crowns him.

major-07-il-carro.name: 7 — The Chariot
major-07-il-carro.Scene: A young noblewoman in elaborate dress rides in an open chariot drawn by two white horses; her posture is upright and dignified.

major-08-la-giustizia.name: 8 — Justice
major-08-la-giustizia.Scene: A woman in grey-blue holds two swords upright; in the background a mounted knight appears.

major-09-il-vecchio.name: 9 — The Hermit
major-09-il-vecchio.Scene: An elderly man in blue robes and a wide-brimmed hat walks with a tall staff; he carries an hourglass in his other hand.

major-10-la-ruota.name: 10 — Wheel of Fortune
major-10-la-ruota.Scene: A blindfolded woman turns a large golden wheel; human figures cling to the wheel at its four positions — rising on the left, at the top, descending on the right, at the bottom.

major-11-la-fortezza.name: 11 — Strength
major-11-la-fortezza.Scene: A youth in a landscape strikes a rearing lion with a club, subduing it through physical force.

major-12-il-traditore.name: 12 — The Hanged Man
major-12-il-traditore.Scene: A figure in a white tunic and green tights hangs upside down by one ankle from a frame; the composition is vertical and the posture is calm despite the inversion.

major-13-la-morte.name: 13 — Death
major-13-la-morte.Scene: A white skeleton stands frontally, facing the viewer, and holds a bow and arrow; the figure is set against a plain gold background.

major-14-la-temperanza.name: 14 — Temperance
major-14-la-temperanza.Scene: A young woman in a blue star-spangled gown pours liquid between two ornate vessels in a careful, steady gesture.

major-15-il-diavolo.name: 15 — The Devil
major-15-il-diavolo.Scene: Card not extant in the surviving Visconti-Sforza deck. Based on the standard 15th-century Italian trump programme, the Devil would have depicted a demonic figure — horned, winged, and dark — presiding over chained figures representing the enslaved passions or spiritual captivity.

major-16-la-torre.name: 16 — The Tower
major-16-la-torre.Scene: Card not extant in the surviving Visconti-Sforza deck. Based on the standard 15th-century Italian trump programme, the Tower would have depicted a tall structure being struck by lightning or fire, with figures falling from it.

major-17-la-stella.name: 17 — The Star
major-17-la-stella.Scene: A standing woman in blue and red robes holds a large gold star aloft in one hand; her posture is upright and ceremonial.

major-18-la-luna.name: 18 — The Moon
major-18-la-luna.Scene: A woman in pink holds a crescent moon; a ribbon or rope extends from her other hand.

major-19-il-sole.name: 19 — The Sun
major-19-il-sole.Scene: A winged cherub or putto flies through the air holding a sun disc with a human face; a landscape appears below.

major-20-il-giudizio.name: 20 — Judgement
major-20-il-giudizio.Scene: Two trumpeting angels flank a central divine figure at the top; below, two human figures rise from a stone sarcophagus, their hands raised.

major-21-il-mondo.name: 21 — The World
major-21-il-mondo.Scene: Two winged putti hold a large circular globe between them; within the globe a walled city or castle is depicted in miniature.

coins-ace.name: Ace of Coins
coins-ace.Scene: A single large coin bearing a heraldic coat of arms is displayed at centre; botanical vines with flowers and foliage fill the card border.

coins-02.name: Two of Coins
coins-02.Scene: Two coins are arranged vertically at centre; a ribbon banner bearing the text 'AIEN DROYE' (a variant of the Visconti motto 'a bon droyt') crosses the card horizontally.

coins-03.name: Three of Coins
coins-03.Scene: Three coins are arranged with two banners bearing a variant motto text; botanical border fills the remaining space.

coins-04.name: Four of Coins
coins-04.Scene: Four coins are arranged in a two-by-two grid; a banner carries the Visconti motto; botanical border fills the card.

coins-05.name: Five of Coins
coins-05.Scene: Five coins are arranged in a quincunx pattern — two above, one at centre, two below; two banner inscriptions carry the motto; botanical border.

coins-06.name: Six of Coins
coins-06.Scene: Six coins are arranged in a two-by-three grid; botanical border with flowers and vines fills the remaining space.

coins-07.name: Seven of Coins
coins-07.Scene: Seven coins are arranged asymmetrically — the count does not resolve into a perfect grid; botanical border.

coins-08.name: Eight of Coins
coins-08.Scene: Eight coins are arranged in a two-by-four formation; botanical border.

coins-09.name: Nine of Coins
coins-09.Scene: Nine coins are arranged in a three-by-three grid; botanical border.

coins-10.name: Ten of Coins
coins-10.Scene: Ten coins are arranged in a two-by-five configuration; botanical border.

coins-page.name: Page of Coins
coins-page.Scene: A youth in an ornate blue and gold cloak stands on a grass ground, looking upward and to the right with an open, wondering expression.

coins-knight.name: Knight of Coins
coins-knight.Scene: A rider in a pink and yellow tunic sits on a white horse against a gold-tooled background; this is a larger-format Cary-Yale card.

coins-queen.name: Queen of Coins
coins-queen.Scene: A woman in a black and gold patterned gown is seated in profile; a large coin rests on her lap.

coins-king.name: King of Coins
coins-king.Scene: A young man in a dark patterned tunic sits on an octagonal throne; he holds a staff in one hand and a coin in the other; his legs are in parti-colored hose.

cups-ace.name: Ace of Cups
cups-ace.Scene: A tall elaborate golden fountain-chalice with an eagle finial at the top stands at centre; botanical vines with flowers and foliage fill the card border.

cups-02.name: Two of Cups
cups-02.Scene: Two ornate chalice cups are arranged vertically at centre; a ribbon banner reads a variant of the Visconti motto.

cups-03.name: Three of Cups
cups-03.Scene: Three cups are arranged in a triangular formation; botanical border.

cups-04.name: Four of Cups
cups-04.Scene: Four cups are arranged in a two-by-two grid; a banner reads the Visconti motto; botanical border.

cups-05.name: Five of Cups
cups-05.Scene: Five cups in a one-plus-two-plus-two arrangement; botanical border.

cups-06.name: Six of Cups
cups-06.Scene: Six cups in a two-by-three arrangement; botanical border.

cups-07.name: Seven of Cups
cups-07.Scene: Seven cups in a one-plus-three-plus-three arrangement; botanical border fills the remaining space.

cups-08.name: Eight of Cups
cups-08.Scene: Eight cups in a complex staggered arrangement across the card; botanical border.

cups-09.name: Nine of Cups
cups-09.Scene: Nine cups densely packed in a three-by-three arrangement; botanical border with less room than earlier cards.

cups-10.name: Ten of Cups
cups-10.Scene: Ten cups densely packed and some touching or partially overlapping; botanical border.

cups-page.name: Page of Cups
cups-page.Scene: A blonde youth in a blue short tunic stands in profile, balancing a small cup on an upturned outstretched palm; gold-tooled background, green grass below.

cups-knight.name: Knight of Cups
cups-knight.Scene: A blonde youth on a golden horse rides in profile; he holds a cup or makes a forward gesture; gold-tooled background.

cups-queen.name: Queen of Cups
cups-queen.Scene: A standing woman in a long dark brocade gown and crown holds a cup adorned with green decoration; gold brocade background; the card shows age-related damage.

cups-king.name: King of Cups
cups-king.Scene: A bearded man in elaborate red and gold brocade robes sits on an ornate throne holding a large cup; a young page or attendant stands at his right side.

swords-ace.name: Ace of Swords
swords-ace.Scene: A single ornate sword with a gold cross-hilt stands vertically at centre; a flowing ribbon banner reading 'awn droyt' spirals around the blue blade; botanical vines with flowers fill the background.

swords-02.name: Two of Swords
swords-02.Scene: Two swords cross in an X formation at centre; a ribbon banner reads the Visconti motto; botanical border.

swords-03.name: Three of Swords
swords-03.Scene: Three swords — two crossed in X plus one upright at centre — form a layered cross shape; a ribbon banner reads the motto; botanical border.

swords-04.name: Four of Swords
swords-04.Scene: Four swords fan outward from the lower centre in a V or upward-radiating pattern; blue lattice stripes with gold diamond lozenges at the intersections; botanical border.

swords-05.name: Five of Swords
swords-05.Scene: Five swords in a starburst or radiating fan pattern; blue stripe lattice with gold-orange diamond lozenges; botanical border.

swords-06.name: Six of Swords
swords-06.Scene: Six swords in three crossed pairs forming a symmetric geometric lattice; botanical border.

swords-07.name: Seven of Swords
swords-07.Scene: Seven swords in a complex interlaced arrangement; blue lattice stripes with gold-orange lozenges; botanical border.

swords-08.name: Eight of Swords
swords-08.Scene: Eight swords form a dense geometric lattice with blue blade stripes and gold-orange diamond fills at all intersections; botanical border.

swords-09.name: Nine of Swords
swords-09.Scene: Nine swords form a very complex dense lattice filling most of the card; gold-orange and green lozenges at intersections; small botanical elements only at the edges.

swords-10.name: Ten of Swords
swords-10.Scene: Ten swords form the most complex interlaced lattice on the card; gold-green and orange lozenges fill the intersections; a minimal botanical border remains.

swords-page.name: Page of Swords
swords-page.Scene: A young person in full silver plate armour stands on green grass holding a long sword point-down at the left side; blonde curly hair is visible above the armour collar; gold patterned background.

swords-knight.name: Knight of Swords
swords-knight.Scene: A rider in full black plate armour on a dark horse holds a long sword upright; an orange-gold cloak is partially visible; green grass below; gold damask background.

swords-queen.name: Queen of Swords
swords-queen.Scene: A woman in a white gown and gold crown is seated in profile; she holds a long sword upright in a dark gauntleted hand; her other hand is slightly raised.

swords-king.name: King of Swords
swords-king.Scene: A crowned figure in full plate armour sits on an octagonal throne; a long sword is held upright in the right hand; a shield leans at the left; the posture is formal and martial.

batons-ace.name: Ace of Batons
batons-ace.Scene: A single tall ornate baton with gold bulbous finials and turned wooden sections stands vertically at centre; a flowing ribbon banner reading 'awn droyt' spirals around it; botanical vines fill the background.

batons-02.name: Two of Batons
batons-02.Scene: Two batons cross in an X formation; a ribbon banner reads the Visconti motto; botanical border.

batons-03.name: Three of Batons
batons-03.Scene: Three batons in a fanned or star arrangement with ribbon banner; botanical border.

batons-04.name: Four of Batons
batons-04.Scene: Four batons in a double-crossed arrangement; ribbon banner; botanical border.

batons-05.name: Five of Batons
batons-05.Scene: Five batons in an arrangement of crossed and fanned staves; ribbon banner reads the motto; botanical border.

batons-06.name: Six of Batons
batons-06.Scene: Six batons in three crossed pairs forming a symmetric arrangement; botanical border.

batons-07.name: Seven of Batons
batons-07.Scene: Seven batons in a symmetric crossed lattice; botanical border.

batons-08.name: Eight of Batons
batons-08.Scene: Eight batons in a symmetric paired lattice; gold-orange diamond lozenges appear at intersections; botanical border.

batons-09.name: Nine of Batons
batons-09.Scene: Nine batons form a complex lattice pattern with gold-orange diamond lozenges at all intersections; small botanical elements at the edges.

batons-10.name: Ten of Batons
batons-10.Scene: Ten batons form the densest lattice, five staves on each side creating a full bilateral arrangement; green and orange lozenges fill the intersections; minimal botanical border remains.

batons-page.name: Page of Batons
batons-page.Scene: A blonde youth in a rich blue cloak with gold-orange trim stands in profile on green grass, holding a tall ornate baton; gold brocade background.

batons-knight.name: Knight of Batons
batons-knight.Scene: A blonde youth in a blue and orange tunic rides a white horse in motion; the horse appears active or in canter; a baton is held upright; gold damask background.

batons-queen.name: Queen of Batons
batons-queen.Scene: A standing woman in a dark blue gown with green brocade sleeves holds a tall baton in her right hand; she stands on an octagonal platform facing forward; gold background.

batons-king.name: King of Batons
batons-king.Scene: A crowned man in a dark blue striped robe and gold hose sits on an octagonal gold throne; his legs are crossed casually at the ankles; he holds a short baton in each green-gloved hand.

emg-trionfi.name: The Trionfi — The 22 Triumphs
emg-trionfi.Scene: The Visconti-Sforza trionfi (triumph cards) are the earliest surviving painted tarot trumps of high artistic quality, produced in Milan circa 1450 for the Sforza family. Each is painted in tempera and gold leaf on thick card, with gilded backgrounds and finely modeled figures in courtly dress. The imagery draws on the allegorical tradition of triumphal processions.

emg-suit-coins.name: Suit of Coins (Denari) — Earth
emg-suit-coins.Scene: The Coins cards of the Visconti-Sforza show gold disc-shaped coins arranged in geometric patterns against the card surface. The suit pips appear as large, clearly rendered medallion forms. Court cards in the Coins suit show standing or mounted figures bearing shields or banners with coin emblems.

emg-suit-cups.name: Suit of Cups (Coppe) — Water
emg-suit-cups.Scene: The Cups cards display ornate chalice or goblet forms as their suit symbol. The cups are rendered as elaborate gold vessels, consistent with the luxury material culture of the Sforza court. Court figures carry or attend to these vessels with ceremonial posture.

emg-suit-swords.name: Suit of Swords (Spade) — Air
emg-suit-swords.Scene: The Swords cards show long straight blades arranged in crossed or stacked patterns. The swords are depicted as real weapons of the period — double-edged, with cross-guards — rather than as symbolic abstractions. Court figures in this suit are shown in martial stance.

emg-suit-batons.name: Suit of Batons (Bastoni) — Fire
emg-suit-batons.Scene: The Batons (also called Staves or Bastoni) cards show thick wooden clubs or rod-like implements arranged across the card face. The batons have a rough, organic quality that distinguishes them from the refined metal suits. Some cards show them knotted or gnarled like natural branches.

emg-lost-cards.name: The Lost Cards
emg-lost-cards.Scene: Six cards of the original Visconti-Sforza deck are missing and were replaced in the eighteenth century by hand-painted facsimiles executed in a different style. The replacement cards — which include The Devil, The Tower, The Star, The Moon, The Sun, and The World — are identifiable by their slightly different scale, color palette, and execution.

emg-second-hand.name: The Restoration Hand — Six Repainted Triumphs
emg-second-hand.Scene: Several cards of the Visconti-Sforza deck show evidence of later intervention — retouching of the gilding, restoration of damaged areas, or overpainting of faces and drapery. These secondary hands are distinguishable from the primary Bembo-workshop execution by differences in line quality and pigment handling.

kw-minor-arcana.name: Minor arcana
kw-minor-arcana.Scene: The minor arcana of the Visconti-Sforza consist of fifty-six painted cards divided into four suits. Each suit pip card shows the suit emblem repeated in a plain arrangement on a gilt or plain background. The court cards are richly painted figures against gilded grounds, consistent in quality with the trionfi.

kw-major-arcana.name: Major arcana
kw-major-arcana.Scene: The major arcana (trionfi) of the Visconti-Sforza are among the oldest surviving tarot trump cards. Painted on thick card with tempera and gold leaf, they depict allegorical and mythological figures in the tradition of the triumph procession. The gold backgrounds give them an iconic, devotional quality distinct from later printed decks.

kw-trionfi.name: Trionfi
kw-trionfi.Scene: In the Visconti-Sforza, the trionfi sequence follows an early unnumbered arrangement. The figures — Fool, Magician, Empress, Emperor, Pope, Love, Chariot, Fortitude, Wheel of Fortune, Hermit, Hanged Man, Death, Temperance, Devil, Tower, Star, Moon, Sun, World, Fame, and Time — are depicted as procession floats or courtly allegories.

kw-court-card.name: Court card
kw-court-card.Scene: Court cards in the Visconti-Sforza show standing figures — knave, knight, queen, and king — against gold-leaf grounds. Each figure wears elaborately detailed clothing with heraldic devices of the Visconti and Sforza families worked into their costume. The figures are frontal or three-quarter, holding their suit attribute.

kw-air.name: Air
kw-air.Scene: The Swords suit in the Visconti-Sforza carries the air quality. The straight, upright blades suggest clarity, intellect, and the cutting edge of discernment.

kw-batons.name: Batons
kw-batons.Scene: The Batons or Staves suit carries a fire quality. The wooden rods are rendered as natural, unfinished implements — close to their organic source — suggesting active, generative energy.

kw-coins.name: Coins
kw-coins.Scene: The Coins or Denari carry an earth quality. The round, weighty gold discs suggest material substance, value, and the density of worldly resource.

kw-cups.name: Cups
kw-cups.Scene: The Cups or Coppe carry a water quality. The chalice forms suggest containment, feeling, and the interior life of emotional experience.

kw-earth.name: Earth
kw-earth.Scene: Cards associated with the earth quality in this deck show weighted, stable compositions. Coins are the primary earth suit, with their disc forms suggesting the solidity of matter and material life.

kw-fire.name: Fire
kw-fire.Scene: Cards associated with the fire quality show upward movement and active posture. The Batons suit carries this energy through its unrefined wooden implements.

kw-swords.name: Swords
kw-swords.Scene: The Swords suit across the Visconti-Sforza deck displays straight blades in formal arrangements. The suit is associated with the air element and with mental and social conflict.

kw-water.name: Water
kw-water.Scene: The Cups suit carries the water quality throughout the Visconti-Sforza. The chalice imagery suggests emotional depth, containment, and the flow of feeling.

kw-bastoni.name: Bastoni
kw-bastoni.Scene: Bastoni is the Italian name for the Batons suit. In the Visconti-Sforza these appear as thick wooden clubs arranged across each pip card. The term bastoni remained standard in Italian-tradition decks.

kw-coppe.name: Coppe
kw-coppe.Scene: Coppe is the Italian name for the Cups suit. In the Visconti-Sforza the coppe are rendered as ornate chalice vessels with elaborate stems and rims, consistent with the goldsmith culture of the Sforza court.

kw-denari.name: Denari
kw-denari.Scene: Denari (coins) is the Italian name for the Coins suit. The denari in the Visconti-Sforza appear as large flat golden discs, clearly rendered to evoke real currency and material worth.

kw-spade.name: Spade
kw-spade.Scene: Spade is the Italian name for the Swords suit. The spade in the Visconti-Sforza are depicted as real weapons — double-edged and cross-guarded — arranged in stacked or crossed formations on the pip cards.

kw-ace.name: Ace
kw-ace.Scene: The Ace cards of each suit in the Visconti-Sforza show a single large suit emblem against a gilt or plain ground, sometimes held by a hand emerging from a cloud — an early example of the hand-from-cloud motif that became standard in later Italian decks.

kw-cavallo.name: Cavallo
kw-cavallo.Scene: Cavallo (the knight on horseback) is one of the four Visconti-Sforza court ranks. The knight card shows a mounted figure in armor carrying the suit attribute on a shield or banner, depicted against a gilded background.

kw-eight.name: Eight
kw-eight.Scene: The Eight pip cards show eight suit emblems arranged in two parallel columns or a loose geometric pattern, suggesting accumulation and density within the suit element.

kw-fante.name: Fante
kw-fante.Scene: Fante (knave or page) is the lowest court rank in the Visconti-Sforza. The fante cards show a standing youthful figure carrying the suit attribute, typically in a tunic and hose against a gilded background.

kw-five.name: Five
kw-five.Scene: The Five pip cards show five emblems in an asymmetrical arrangement — two pairs and one isolated element — giving the fives a slightly unbalanced quality compared to the even-numbered cards.

kw-four.name: Four
kw-four.Scene: The Four pip cards show four emblems in a balanced square or two-by-two arrangement, giving them a stable, symmetrical character.

kw-king.name: King
kw-king.Scene: The King cards (Re) show a crowned, seated or standing figure of authority in full court dress, bearing the suit attribute and surrounded by heraldic details of the Visconti-Sforza household.

kw-knight.name: Knight
kw-knight.Scene: The Knight cards (Cavallo) show a mounted figure in armor, the most dynamic of the court figures. The horse and rider together convey movement and martial energy.

kw-nine.name: Nine
kw-nine.Scene: The Nine pip cards show nine emblems arranged in three rows of three, giving them a sense of abundance and near-completion within the suit.

kw-page.name: Page
kw-page.Scene: Page cards (Fante) show standing youthful figures, the attendants of the court. They hold their suit attribute forward, as if presenting or offering it.

kw-queen.name: Queen
kw-queen.Scene: The Queen cards (Regina) show a seated or standing female figure in elaborate court dress with a crown or headdress, holding or attended by the suit attribute.

kw-re.name: Re
kw-re.Scene: Re (king) is the highest court rank in Italian-tradition decks. The Re cards of the Visconti-Sforza show crowned figures in full majesty, often with heraldic devices of the Sforza family incorporated into their robes.

kw-regina.name: Regina
kw-regina.Scene: Regina (queen) is the female court rank in the Visconti-Sforza. The regina cards show crowned or veiled female figures in rich brocade dress, holding the suit attribute with a formal, composed bearing.

kw-seven.name: Seven
kw-seven.Scene: The Seven pip cards show seven emblems in an irregular arrangement, carrying a sense of movement or incompleteness that distinguishes them from the stable sixes.

kw-six.name: Six
kw-six.Scene: The Six pip cards arrange six emblems in two parallel columns of three, creating a balanced and visually resolved composition.

kw-ten.name: Ten
kw-ten.Scene: The Ten pip cards show ten suit emblems filling the card space, giving the impression of abundance and culmination at the end of the numbered sequence.

kw-three.name: Three
kw-three.Scene: The Three pip cards show three emblems in a triangular arrangement, suggesting initial expansion and the first dynamic grouping beyond the pair.

kw-two.name: Two
kw-two.Scene: The Two pip cards show a pair of suit emblems, often mirrored or balanced, suggesting duality, exchange, and the beginning of relationship within the suit.

axis-keyword.name: By Keyword
axis-keyword.Scene: Browse the Visconti-Sforza by keyword — suit, element, number, court rank, and thematic grouping.
